subject: history
title: The Decolonisation Chain in Southeast Asia

questions.prompt: A student says: Each colony won independence on its own, because what happened in a neighbouring territory made no difference to nationalist pressure at home. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - each territory had its own leaders and parties, so nothing that happened next door can have mattered

The territories were linked by a chain: independence in one raised nationalist pressure in the next, because campaigners could point to a neighbour that had already won, colonial control weakened stage by stage, and the example was carried on - Philippines 1946, Indonesia recognised 1949, Malaya 1957, Singapore internal self-government 1959.
The territories all won independence in the same year, so they must have acted as one movement
Only the Philippines mattered; the other territories were granted independence for unrelated trade reasons

questions.misconception: Each colony won independence on its own, because what happened in a neighbouring territory made no difference to nationalist pressure at home.
questions.explanation: The trap claim is: Each colony won independence on its own, because what happened in a neighbouring territory made no difference to nationalist pressure at home. In fact The territories were linked by a chain: independence in one raised nationalist pressure in the next, because campaigners could point to a neighbour that had already won, colonial control weakened stage by stage, and the example was carried on - Philippines 1946, Indonesia recognised 1949, Malaya 1957, Singapore internal self-government 1959.

questions.prompt: In which year was Indonesian independence recognised?
questions.explanation: Scene 2 works this: the Philippine example raises pressure in Indonesia, and the Netherlands recognises Indonesian independence in 1949.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state the four stages of the decolonisation chain in order.
questions.answer: Philippines independence in 1946, Indonesia recognised in 1949, Malaya independence in 1957, and Singapore internal self-government in 1959.
questions.explanation: The animation runs the chain in that order, with a transmission arrow carrying the example from each stage to the next.

questions.prompt: Explain why nationalist pressure in Malaya started from a stronger position than pressure in the Philippines had.
questions.answer: By the time Malaya campaigned, two neighbours - the Philippines (1946) and Indonesia (recognised 1949) - had already won, so campaigners could point to living proof that independence could be won, and colonial control had already weakened stage by stage.
questions.explanation: Scene 3 shows the pressure bar rising with the examples of two independent neighbours behind it, while the control bar keeps falling.

questions.prompt: Which list gives the decolonisation chain in order?

choices.text: Philippines 1946, Indonesia recognised 1949, Malaya 1957, Singapore internal self-government 1959

questions.explanation: The whole animation names the chain: one territory wins, the example is carried on, pressure rises in the next - Philippines, Indonesia, Malaya, Singapore.
